questions.q: What does colon notation like `v:CIK` do?
options: Pulls a named top-level field out of a VARIANT value
Deletes a field from a VARIANT value
Renames a column permanently in the underlying table
Converts a VARIANT column into a CSV file
questions.explain: Colon notation reaches into a VARIANT value and returns the named field's value.

questions.q: Why do you almost always add a `::type` cast after a colon-notation lookup, like `v:CIK::string`?
options: Because the raw colon-notation result comes back typed as VARIANT, not a concrete SQL type
Because casting is required by Snowflake's licensing terms
Because colon notation only works on already-cast columns
Casting is optional and has no real effect on the result
questions.explain: Without a cast, the value stays VARIANT-typed; casting to ::string, ::date, ::number, etc. gives you a usable, concrete type.

questions.q: How do you reach a nested field, like a city inside an address object, using this lesson's notation?
options: Chain colons: v:address:city::string
Nested fields cannot be queried in Snowflake
Use a separate FLATTEN statement — colon notation never supports nesting
Use v.address.city with dots only, never colons
questions.explain: Colon notation chains for nested objects, e.g. v:address:city::string, similar to dot-chaining in JavaScript or Python.

Converting a VARIANT column back into a plain string permanently
Deleting all JSON formatting from a column
Merging two VARIANT columns into one
questions.explain: PARSE_JSON turns a JSON-formatted string into a real VARIANT, which you can then query the same way as a native VARIANT column.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why do teams typically wrap a VARIANT table in a view with colon-notation SELECTs instead of querying the raw VARIANT table everywhere?
options: So downstream queries just see plain, typed columns and never need to know the data started life as JSON
Because Snowflake refuses to allow more than one query against a VARIANT table
Because views run computations faster than any other SQL object type
Because VARIANT columns can only be queried once per session
questions.explain: A view applies the colon/dot notation and casts once, so every downstream query sees ordinary typed columns instead of repeating VARIANT syntax.
